title: Finite module generators bounded by fibre dimensions
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with finitely many maximal ideals, $A$ a commutative $R$-algebra which is finitely generated as an $R$-module, and $n\in\mathbb N$. For a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, let $\kappa(\mathfrak m)$ be the fraction field of $R/\mathfrak m$ and let $A(\mathfrak m)=\kappa(\mathfrak m)\otimes_R A$. If $\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak m)} A(\mathfrak m)\le n$ for every maximal ideal, there is a surjective $R$-linear map $R^n\to A$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00DV (parts 6 and 8), used in Morphisms Tag 03J6

proof.text: For each maximal ideal p choose a basis of kappa(p) tensor_R A, and extend the list by zeros to length n. This is legitimate because A is finite over R, so the fibre is finite-dimensional. The canonical R-algebra map R/p to kappa(p) is an isomorphism because p is maximal (Ideal.bijective_algebraMap_quotient_residueField).

Distinct maximal ideals are coprime. The Chinese remainder map R to the product of R/p is surjective with kernel J=intersection p. Tensor this exact sequence with A. Right exactness and the finite product tensor identity give surjectivity of A to the product of fibre modules and identify its kernel with J A; these are implemented by Ideal.pi_tensorProductMk_quotient_surjective and Ideal.ker_tensorProductMk_quotient. Thus each of the n columns of the spanning families lifts simultaneously to an element v_i of A.

For any element x of the product of the fibre modules, write each component as a linear combination of its n padded basis vectors. The ring Chinese remainder map lifts the coefficients for each i simultaneously to r_i in R. Then the image of sum_i r_i v_i is x. Hence the span N of the v_i satisfies A=N+J A.

J is contained in the Jacobson radical by its definition as the intersection of the maximal ideals. The finite module A/N satisfies J(A/N)=A/N, so Nakayama makes A/N zero. Equivalently N=A; the implementation uses Submodule.le_of_le_smul_of_le_jacobson_bot, the submodule form of the same lemma. The linear combination map R^n to A is therefore surjective. For n=0 this says A=0. For R the zero ring, the maximal spectrum is empty and all R-modules are zero; the same proof applies.

proof_origin.place: Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK), parts 4 and 8, combined with Chinese remainder lifting as the semilocal version of the generator argument in Tag 03J6.
